key_insight: DynaFLIP moves motion understanding into the perception stage itself, instead of relying on downstream robot policies to infer dynamics later. By aligning image, language, and 3D flow signals, it learns representations that better capture action-relevant scene changes.
problem_solved: Most robot perception backbones are trained for static recognition or vision-language matching, which can miss the motion and dynamics needed for manipulation. This paper addresses the gap between visual understanding and action-relevant dynamics in robot learning.
method: Builds tri-modal pretraining data from image-language-3D flow triplets collected from heterogeneous human and robot sources.
Learns a dynamics-aware multimodal representation that explicitly incorporates motion cues during perception pretraining.
Guides the model to preserve action-relevant structure in the scene so downstream manipulation policies can use more informative features.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in robotics, DynaFLIP suggests a stronger perception foundation for manipulation tasks by encoding motion early. This can improve generalization and reduce the burden on downstream policies to discover dynamics from scratch.
visual_elements: A tri-modal pipeline diagram showing image, language, and 3D flow inputs merging into one representation.

paper_title: DynaFLIP: Rethinking Robotics Perception via Tri-Modal-Dynamics Guided Representation
paper_authors: Jusuk Lee, Seungjae Lee, Jonghun Shin, Hoseong Jung, Sungha Kim
